person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: All of these mnemonic effects on neuronal responses bias the competitive interactions that take place between stimulus representations in the cortex when there is more than one stimulus in the visual field.

span.label: repetition suppression (neural repetition priming)
span.quote: Fig. 1 summarizes in a diagrammatic fashion some of the cortical mechanisms for visual memory that appear to impact on attentional selection processes.

span.label: review
span.quote: We have considered only three short-term memory mechanisms in this brief review, namely repetition suppression, enhancement, and delay activity.

span.label: Only three short-term mechanisms are covered; long-term plasticity and perceptual learning are left out.
span.quote: These are hardly exhaustive, and, in particular, we have not touched on known mechanisms for long-term plasticity and perceptual learning.

span.label: Hippocampal and medial temporal lobe memory (events, maps, scenes, episodes) is explicitly outside the scope.
span.quote: The types of memories normally associated with the hippocampus and medial temporal lobe structures, including memories of more complex behavioral events, maps, scenes, episodes, etc., are not considered.

span.label: The direct test of whether prefrontal feedback causes the IT match-enhancement effect has not been performed.
span.quote: This experiment has not yet been done, but Fuster et al. ( 47 ) have recorded delay activity in IT cortex during cooling of prefrontal cortex.

span.label: contradicts → studies reporting that IT cells hold a sample stimulus in memory through stimulus-selective maintained delay activity (refs 27-33)
span.quote: We found counter-evidence for this idea, however, in our studies using the DMS task with multiple nonmatch test stimuli intervening between the sample and the matching test ( 31 ).

span.label: extends → Nakamura and Kubota (ref 33)
span.quote: This result explains an otherwise contradictory report from Nakamura and Kubota ( 33 ), who found that cells in the anterior and temporal polar regions of IT cortex had stimulus-specific maintained activity in the delays following the sample in a delayed nonmatch-to-sample task.

span.label: neurons respond less to repeated than to novel stimuli (repetition suppression)
span.quote: Repetition suppression appears to be an intrinsic property of visual cortical areas such as inferior temporal cortex and is thought to be important for perceptual learning and priming
